s: affirmation; assurance; the act of assuring someone
to insure (to provide for compensation if some specified risk occurs)

Which health insurance company are you insured under?

She would like to insure her housegood goods against fire.
to reassure, assure: [with dative ‘someone’ and accusative ‘about something’]
He reassures her of his love.
Ich versichere Ihnen, dass wir alles tun, um ihn zu finden.
Let me assure you that we are doing everything to find him.
to reassure, assure: [with genitive ‘about something’ or dass (+ clause) ‘that ...’]
Ich wollte mich Ihrer Unterstützung versichern.
I wanted to assure myself of your support.
Zunächst einmal muss ich mich versichern, dass du das wirklich willst.
First of all, I need to make (myself) sure that you really want this.
to reassure, assure: [with accusative ‘someone’, along with genitive ‘about something’ or dass (+ clause) ‘that ...’]
He reassures her of his love.
Ich versichere Sie, dass wir alles tun, um ihn zu finden.
Let me assure you that we are doing everything to find him.
to take possession of, to secure
Der Spion versicherte sich der geheimen Dokumente und flüchtete in die Berge.
The spy secured the secret documents and fled into the mountains.
versichern.et: From Middle High German versichern. Equivalen to ver- + sichern. The insurance sense (17th c.) is a calque of Italian assicurare.

versifizieren.et: From Latin versificare. Equivalent to Vers + -fizieren.

s: sealing (e.g. of a document with a signet to indicate authorship, approval, etc)
sealing to discourage or make noticeable unauthorized opening of (something, e.g. a letter, or a building)
sealing (e.g. of a leak in a pipe)
the waterproof "sealing" of the earth's surface by human constructions
Versiegelung.et: From the verb versiegeln (to seal), from siegeln, from the noun Siegel (seal) + the noun suffix -ung

versinken.et: From Middle High German versinken, from Old High German firsinkan, firsincan. Equivalent to ver- + sinken.

s: to realize (convert an asset into cash)
silver plate, the silver applied after silvering
to become filthy, dirty, especially with moist or greasy dirt (hence often said e.g. of bathrooms or kitchens)
versiffen.et: Equivalent to ver- + Siff (“filth”) + -en, though the noun may in fact be a backformation from the verb. See Siff for more.

s: to seep in, to seep away
Der größte Teil des Wassers ist im Boden versickert
Most of the water has seeped into the ground.
to disappear slowly, to wane away slowly

versiegeln.et: From Middle High German versigelen, from Old High German firsigilen. Equivalent to ver- + siegeln.

versiegen.et: From the past participle of verseihen.

s: to septuple, to septuplicate, to multiply by seven
to increase sevenfold (to become seven times as large)
Die Bevölkerung hat sich inzwischen versiebenfacht.
Meanwhile the population has increased sevenfold.
versiebenfachen.et: siebenfach + ver- -en. See ver- -fachen for more.
